message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | ~1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.0899 g/L (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121.5 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Specific heat capacity | 14.304 J/(mol·K) |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L/mol |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –72.8 kJ/mol |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Bond type | Covalent (diatomic H₂) |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| | Reactivity | Forms hydrides with metals; reacts with halogens, oxygen, acids, and many other compounds |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (forming H⁺) or base (forming H⁻ as hydride) depending on context |
| **Molecular Characteristics** | Molecular weight | 2.016 g/mol (H₂) |
| | Bond length (H₂) | 0.74 Å |
| | Bond energy (H₂) | 436 kJ/mol |
| | Dipole moment | 0 (homonuclear diatomic) |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman, Balmer series in UV/visible |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Most abundant, stable |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, heavier isotope used in NMR, heavy water |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life ~12.32 y), used in nuclear fusion research |
| **Applications & Significance** | Energy carrier | Fuel cell technology, rocket propellant |
| | Chemical synthesis | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, etc. |
| | Biological role | Essential component of water, organic molecules, and metabolic processes |
| | Astrophysics | Dominant element in stars; hydrogen burning powers the Sun |
| | Environmental impact | Hydrogen combustion produces only water vapor (clean energy source) |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Hydrogen is the simplest element**: one proton, one electron, and no neutrons in its most common isotope (protium).
- **It exists as a diatomic gas (H₂)** under normal conditions, but can form various compounds (hydrides, acids, organics).
- **Its physical properties make it light, colorless, and highly flammable**, which is why it’s used in fuel cells and rockets but requires careful handling.
- **Isotopic variants (deuterium, tritium)** have distinct nuclear properties useful in scientific research and energy applications.
- **Hydrogen’s role in chemistry and physics** is foundational—from forming water to powering stars—making it a cornerstone of both life and the universe.
